How to Handle Shipping Exceptions

Responsible Teams and Roles
Operations Specialists, Fulfillment Leads, Customer Support

Shipping Exception Workflow Runbook

Purpose
This runbook provides the shipping exception workflow for handling delays, address problems, damaged parcels, and returned-to-sender events. It helps teams act consistently while minimizing customer frustration and unnecessary cost.

When to Use
Use this runbook when carrier tracking, warehouse alerts, or customer contacts indicate a shipment has deviated from the expected delivery path.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: Operations Specialist.
Supporting roles: Fulfillment Lead, Customer Support, Carrier Relations.
Approver: Operations Manager for costly exceptions or unusual recovery actions.

Procedure
Step 1: Confirm the tracking number, order value, service level, and most recent carrier scan.
Step 2: Classify the issue as delay, address problem, damage, return-to-sender, or delivered-not-received.
Step 3: Review the order promise date, customer impact, and whether proactive outreach is required.
Step 4: Determine whether the package should be monitored, intercepted, replaced, refunded, or escalated to Claims.
Step 5: Contact the carrier or open a trace if carrier action is needed under service rules.
Step 6: If replacement inventory is limited or the order value is high, obtain manager approval before committing to a recovery option.
Step 7: Update the customer with what happened, what action is in progress, and when the next update will be sent.
Step 8: Record follow-up deadlines so no shipment exception remains unattended across shifts.
Step 9: Complete the approved recovery action, such as reshipment, refund, or wait-and-monitor closure.
Step 10: Log any recurring carrier or warehouse root cause for weekly operational review.

Approval Requirements
High-value replacements or refunds require Operations Manager approval.
Potential fraud or abuse indicators require Risk or Claims consultation.
Returned-to-sender reshipments caused by warehouse error may be approved without extra customer charge once root cause is confirmed.

Completion Criteria
The shipping exception case is complete when the recovery path is executed, the customer has final confirmation, and all operational notes are captured.
